To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MaSCs in the mouse mammary gland are highly enriched in CD49fhi basal cells, and (2) these cells are also enriched in the CD24+/mod/S ca-1- subset, and (3) the CD49f hi/CD29 hi/CD24+/ mod/Sca-1-subset is highly enriched in MaSCs.

the mammary epithelial cells with in vivo repopulation ability reside within the CD24+/mod/S1/Sca-1-/CD29hi/ CD49fhi population, and that this subset contains the majority of the cells that have a long-term self-renewal potential.

the mammary gland contains a rare population of stem cells that are enriched in the basal cell compartment, that can be prospectively purified and that can be transplanted into cleared mammary fatpads where they give rise to a complete mammary gland.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biology of the mammary stem cell.

the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the activity of MaSCs in vivo, and with the role of these cells in mammary carcinogenesis and in the development of resistance to chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
the identification of the molecular pathways that control the self-renewal of MaSCs and their commitment to the myoepithelium or luminal lineages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MaSCs are defined as CD49fhiCD29hiCD24+/modSca-1- cells.
the in vivo transplantation model has been instrumental in identifying the MaSCs as a highly enriched population within the basal epithelial cell population, which can be prospectively purified.
the CD49f/CD29hi basal cell subpopulations contain a small proportion of cells that have the capacity to regenerate a complete mammary gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MaSC assay in vivo has been used to define and characterize a stem cell population that has been shown to have the ability to generate all the lineages in the mammary gland.
MaSCs have been defined as a population that is enriched in a subset of basal mammary cells that have the ability to generate all the cell types of the mammary gland.

we have been able to identify and purify a population of stem cells from the mammary gland of mice that are able to generate complex, fully functional mammary glands in a single transplantation assay.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MaSCs can be identified in the CD49fh basal population by their capacity to regenerate the mammary gland in vivo, and that the CD49fh/CD24+/Sca-1- population represents the most highly enriched subset.
the CD24+ population is highly enriched in MaSCs.
the CD24+/mod/S ca-1- population is heterogeneous.
